EDA of category and store_location:

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(walmart, aes(x = store_location, fill = category)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", color = "black")+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Appliances" = "purple",
    "Electronics" = "red"
  ))+
  labs(title = "Number of Transactions by Store Location and Category",
    x = "Store Location",
    y = "Number of Transactions",
    fill = "Category")

EDA of category and customer_income:

ggplot(walmart, aes(x = category, y=customer_income)) +

  labs(title="Box plot of Customer Income in Walmart using `ggplot`", x="", y = "Customer Income(Dollar Amount)")

The data looks pretty similar across both appliances and electronics.

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data=walmart, aes(customer_income)) + 
  geom_histogram(breaks=seq(20005.34, 119999.8, by = 2000),
                 col="black", 
                 fill="gold", 
                 alpha = .8) + # opacity
  labs(x="Customer Income(Dollar Amount)", y="Frequency") +
  labs(title="Histogram of Customer Income for Walmart Dataset using `ggplot`")

qqnorm(walmart$customer_income, main="Q-Q plot of Customer Income in Walmart") 
qqline(walmart$customer_income)

The distribution for the customer_income as a whole is approximately uniform with no strong skewing.

Chi Square Test of store_location and category

contableSL = table(walmart$category, walmart$store_location)
xkabledply(contableSL, title="Contingency table for category and store_location within walmart dataset")
Contingency table for category and store_location within walmart dataset
Chicago, IL Dallas, TX Los Angeles, CA Miami, FL New York, NY
Appliances 490 491 467 469 498
Electronics 523 507 571 495 489

Test of Independence on category and store_location on contable

Null Hypothesis: Category and store_location are independent

Alternative Hypothesis: Category and store_location are not independent

Alpha = 0.05

chitestSL = chisq.test(contableSL)
chitestSL
## 
##  Pearson's Chi-squared test
## 
## data:  contableSL
## X-squared = 6.7627, df = 4, p-value = 0.149

Conclusion: Since the p-value(0.1489722) is greater than the alpha(0.05) we can conclude that we cannot reject the null hypothesis. Which provides evidence suggesting that store_location and category are independent.

T-Test of customer_income and category

Customer_income Null Hypothesis: means are equal for appliances and electronics

Customer_income Alternative Hypothesis: means are not equal for appliances and electronics

Alpha = 0.05

ttestCI = t.test(appliances$customer_income, electronics$customer_income)
ttestCI
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  appliances$customer_income and electronics$customer_income
## t = 1.3643, df = 4990.2, p-value = 0.1725
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -489.6096 2730.8529
## sample estimates:
## mean of x mean of y 
##  70620.99  69500.37

Conclusion: Since the p-value(0.1725206) is less than the alpha(0.05) we can conclude by failing to reject the null hypothesis. Which provides evidence suggesting that the mean value of customer_income for appliances is equal to electronics
